rollups.text: Sneakers Darryl bought or owned: Adidas Ultraboost, size 11, ordered April 1, 2024 for $153 after a $27 discount from $180; size 11.5 reordered May 1 and returned June 12 for a $153 refund because of fit issues; limited-edition New Balance 990v5 “Montserrat Blue,” acquired by June 20, 2024 for $250 and tried in size 10.5 on June 14; limited-edition Nike Dunk Low “Montserrat Pride,” bought July 30, 2024 for $300 and delivered August 3 at 10:15 AM by DHL Express. Darryl reported owning five pairs on June 20, seven pairs on August 5, and described the Dunk Low purchase as his first limited-edition purchase despite his earlier 990v5 acquisition.

Sneaker models repeatedly discussed for Darryl: Adidas Ultraboost/UltraBoost DNA; Nike Air Max 270 and Air Max 270 React; Nike React Infinity Run; Nike Air VaporMax; Nike Air Force 1; Nike Air Zoom Pegasus 38; Brooks Ghost, especially Ghost 14; New Balance Fresh Foam 1080v11, 574, and 990v5; Saucony Ride ISO 4 and Ride 14; Adidas Terrex Free Hiker; Salomon X Ultra 3 GTX; Merrell Moab 2; Vasque Breeze/Breeze II GTX; Keen Targhee III; ASICS Gel-Kayano 28; Adidas Solar Boost; Adidas Superstar; Allbirds and Allbirds Wool Runner/Tree Dasher; Puma RS-X and Puma Suede; Converse Chuck Taylor All Star/All Star Pro; Vans Old Skool; Saucony Jazz Original and Grid ZX; Adidas Stan Smith; Nike Air Max 90; Nike Dunk Low “Montserrat Pride.” Considered, recommended, or discussed across 2024; not all were purchased.

Places and sneaker-related outings: Foot Locker on Main Street in East Janethaven was planned for March 16, 2024, first at 3 PM and later possibly 4 PM; Darryl tried Adidas Ultraboost and Nike React Infinity Run there on March 30 and chose Ultraboost. He visited Foot Locker again May 3 at 4 PM to try Brooks Ghost 14, and tried New Balance 990v5 there on June 14, finding size 10.5 a perfect fit. Darryl and Lauren attended a sneaker art exhibit at the Montserrat Museum on June 16. Darryl walked rocky trails near Soufrière Hills and planned a four-mile round-trip hike on Oriole Trail in June. Sneaker events at East Janethaven Community Center and a sneaker swap were discussed, but attendance was not confirmed.

People connected to Darryl’s sneaker discussions: Lauren is Darryl’s romantic partner, likes minimalist designs and Allbirds, complimented his Brooks Ghost shoes, and attended the Montserrat Museum sneaker art exhibit with him on June 16, 2024. Maureen and Fred are Darryl’s parents; Maureen values durability, and Fred showed interest in sneaker culture. Bradley, age 42, recommended Brooks Ghost at a gym meeting on March 20 and invited Darryl to a sneaker event; he also advised buying protector spray. Christopher, age 42 and a marathon runner, recommended Brooks Ghost for arch support and taught Darryl heel-to-toe running form on May 7. Kyle was described in earlier records as a sneaker-savvy friend, but Darryl later said he had never met anyone like Kyle and had never attended sneaker expos, correcting that account; later records again describe Kyle as a friend and mention his advice and cleaning session with Darryl.

Adidas Ultraboost purchase and fit timeline: On March 30, 2024, Darryl tried Ultraboost and Nike React Infinity Run at Foot Locker and chose Ultraboost. He ordered size 11 online from Finish Line on April 1 for $153 with coupon SPRING15. On April 2 he reported a comfortable three-mile walk and breathable-feeling Primeknit, but remained concerned about fit and returns. By April 30 he experienced slight heel slippage; on May 1 he reordered size 11.5 and considered returning size 11. He returned size 11.5 on June 12 for a $153 refund because of fit issues. The purchase-to-refund period was about 72 days; ordering the larger size did not resolve the fit issue.

Running development and shoe choice: Darryl planned to run three miles by May 1, 2024. On May 6 he jogged two miles in Brooks Ghost and liked the softer DNA LOFT cushioning; Christopher taught him heel-to-toe form on May 7. Darryl completed his first three-mile run on May 8 in 28 minutes, two minutes faster than his target, and reported an 8% pace improvement after learning the technique on May 10. He reported shin-splint concerns and considered changing to Brooks Ghost; after a comfortable three-mile run with no discomfort or fatigue, he decided Brooks Ghost would be for running and Adidas Ultraboost for casual wear. From the May 1 target to the first three-mile run took seven days.

Darryl’s sneaker collection goal: On June 20, 2024, Darryl said he owned five pairs and wanted eight by year-end, meaning three additions. On August 5 he reported seven pairs, or 87.5% of the goal, and was considering an eighth pair. He said the addition would put his budget $50 over, though savings could cover it. The records do not confirm that he acquired an eighth pair by year-end.

Nike Dunk Low “Montserrat Pride” timeline: Darryl bought the limited-edition pair for $300 on July 30, 2024; it featured local artist Simone Clarke’s artwork and had released July 25. Delivery was August 3 at 10:15 AM via DHL Express. On August 5 Darryl decided not to sell immediately, instead keeping the shoes pristine and posting about them on social media while monitoring resale response. He planned to wear them to a film festival and use orthotic insoles; a cleaning/protection session with Kyle was scheduled for August 7. He described the $300 price as $50 above his usual budget but worthwhile for exclusivity, and used a $20 Finish Line gift card.
rollups.topic: limited-edition Dunk purchase and resale decision

rollups.text: Film festival plans: Darryl planned to attend a film festival on August 20, 2024, and considered wearing his Nike Dunk Low “Montserrat Pride”; he and Lauren planned matching sneakers. He hoped showcasing his style would increase his social-media followers by 15%. A separate record refers to a festival on August 22 and asks for a comfortable, stylish outfit; the conversation does not establish whether this was the same event. Suggestions for August 22 included Adidas Ultraboost 21, Nike Air Max 270 React, New Balance 990v5, and Converse Chuck Taylor All Star Pro, but Darryl did not select one.

Sneaker cleaning kit: Darryl planned to meet Kyle at East Janethaven Mall on May 9, 2024, to buy a SneakerLab kit, but purchase was not confirmed. On May 10 he described the kit as normally $25 and discounted 20% to $20 through May 15; a later discussion mentioned an extension through May 20. By June 20 Darryl expected a kit delivery by 3 PM on June 22 and asked what to do if it was late. The records do not confirm whether the kit arrived.

Reported sneaker spending and budgets changed over time: Darryl set a $200 sneaker budget on March 12, 2024. On June 20 he reported spending $575 that year, described a $600 annual budget with $25 remaining, and separately considered a new purchase under an increased $650 budget. On August 5 he again reported $575 spent against a $650 limit; the $300 Dunk Low purchase was described as $50 above his usual budget, and he considered an eighth pair that would put the budget $50 over. These budget figures appear in different contexts and are not fully reconciled.

Darryl’s daily-step challenge: He aimed to reach 10,000 steps each day by April 15, 2024. On April 2 he reported completing 10,000 steps daily for five consecutive days and improving endurance by 12%.

Darryl’s stated sneaker-purchase decision changes: On March 12 he was leaning toward Nike Air Max 270 and planned to size up half a size; after trying shoes on March 30, he chose Adidas Ultraboost over Nike React Infinity Run. He later reordered Ultraboost in a larger size because of heel slippage, then returned the larger pair for fit issues on June 12. By May 10 he had decided to use Brooks Ghost for running and Ultraboost for casual wear. On June 20 he remained undecided about the best daily-wear sneaker.

Darryl’s recurring sneaker preferences and information requests: he wants comfortable shoes for daily wear and city/set walking, sleek modern styling in neutral colors—especially black or gray—and detailed feature comparisons. He has mild flat feet and has repeatedly prioritized medium arch support, later identifying arch support as especially important. He values breathability and moisture management for Montserrat’s tropical climate, durable soles and traction for uneven terrain, and health benefits when features are discussed. On June 20 he asked that sustainability features always be mentioned when discussing sneaker materials. He also asked that delivery details be included for online orders and that event dates be confirmed for upcoming plans.

Darryl reported fit-related return or reorder activity for Adidas Ultraboost in 2024: size 11 caused slight heel slippage, prompting a size 11.5 reorder on May 1; the size 11.5 pair was returned June 12 for fit issues and a $153 refund. In June he said he generally had not returned or reordered sneakers for fit issues before this recent experience.
